detailed_summary: This paper applies the rate operator quantum jumps (ROQJ) method to engineer non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with PT symmetry in an open three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer subject to non-local dephasing. The ROQJ framework allows one to modify the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian governing the no-jump trajectory of an open quantum system by choosing different rate operators, each corresponding to a continuous measurement scheme. The authors use this flexibility to construct a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with a general two-parameter imaginary diagonal part, generalizing the standard gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. They then analyze the spectrum and symmetry structure as a function of on-site interaction strength. For vanishing on-site interaction, they identify an unbroken PT-symmetry region bounded by second-order exceptional lines of different character and four fourth-order exceptional points, two of which are absent in the usual gain-loss model. They also find regions where the imaginary parts of the eigenvalues are degenerate, a feature not present in the gain-loss dimer. Using time-dependent rate operator transformations, they study state transfer under slowly varying parameter loops. Loops encircling a fourth-order exceptional point yield chiral state transfer, but because the loops cross exceptional lines, the final states are superpositions of eigenstates. Chiral state transfer is also observed with non-zero homogeneous on-site interaction when the loop crosses broken PT-symmetry regions of different character. With inhomogeneous on-site interactions, they find direction-dependent state transfer between eigenstates without crossing or encircling exceptional points.
key_contributions: Demonstrates that the ROQJ method can be used to engineer a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with a general two-parameter imaginary diagonal part in the three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer, extending beyond the standard gain-loss configuration.

Characterizes the exceptional point structure for vanishing on-site interaction, revealing an unbroken PT-symmetry region bounded by second-order exceptional lines and four fourth-order exceptional points, two of which are novel compared to the gain-loss dimer.
Identifies regions of degenerate imaginary parts of eigenvalues that do not appear in the conventional gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer.

Shows that time-dependent rate operator transformations enable chiral state transfer when loops encircle a fourth-order exceptional point, and that the final states are superpositions due to crossing exceptional lines.

Finds direction-dependent state transfer between eigenstates using inhomogeneous on-site interactions without crossing or encircling exceptional points, expanding the toolbox for non-Hermitian state control.
methodology_analysis: The authors employ the rate operator quantum jumps (ROQJ) formalism to unravel the master equation of an open quantum system into stochastic pure-state trajectories. By post-selecting on no jumps, the dynamics are governed by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian that can be tailored via the choice of rate operators. This allows the construction of a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with a two-parameter imaginary diagonal part, generalizing the gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. The analysis proceeds by examining the spectrum and symmetry properties as a function of on-site interaction strength, identifying exceptional points and their orders. For state transfer, they use time-dependent rate operator transformations to implement slowly varying parameter loops, studying the resulting chiral dynamics and final state superpositions. The approach combines analytical spectral analysis with numerical simulations of the non-Hermitian dynamics.
results_analysis: For vanishing on-site interaction, the authors find an unbroken PT-symmetry region enclosed by second-order exceptional lines of different character and four fourth-order exceptional points, two of which are not present in the standard gain-loss dimer. They also report regions where the imaginary parts of the eigenvalues are degenerate, a feature absent in the gain-loss model. Under slowly varying parameter loops, loops encircling a fourth-order exceptional point produce chiral state transfer, but because the loops cross exceptional lines, the final states are superpositions of eigenstates. Chiral state transfer is also observed with non-zero homogeneous on-site interaction when the loop crosses broken PT-symmetry regions of different character. With inhomogeneous on-site interactions, direction-dependent state transfer between eigenstates occurs without crossing or encircling exceptional points.
strengths: Provides a systematic extension of the gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer to a more general PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian using the ROQJ method, revealing novel exceptional point structures.
Combines spectral analysis with dynamical state transfer protocols, demonstrating chiral and direction-dependent transfer effects.
Clearly identifies new features such as fourth-order exceptional points and degenerate imaginary parts that are absent in simpler models.
limitations: The analysis is largely numerical and specific to the three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer; scalability to larger systems or different models is not addressed.
The state transfer protocols rely on slowly varying parameter loops (adiabatic approximation), which may be challenging to implement experimentally.
The role of quantum jumps and measurement backaction in the full stochastic dynamics is not fully explored; the focus is on the no-jump trajectory.
connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics, particularly open quantum systems and non-Hermitian physics. It advances the understanding of PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and exceptional points, which are central to studies of non-Hermitian quantum mechanics and topological state transfer. The use of the ROQJ method connects to quantum measurement and decoherence, offering a way to engineer effective non-Hermitian dynamics via continuous monitoring. The results on chiral state transfer and direction-dependent transfer could inspire applications in quantum control and sensing.
overall_assessment: The paper presents a novel and technically sound study that extends the application of the ROQJ method to engineer PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonians in a three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer. The discovery of new exceptional point structures and degenerate imaginary parts, along with the demonstration of chiral and direction-dependent state transfer, constitutes a significant contribution to non-Hermitian quantum physics. The work is well-motivated and the results are clearly presented, though the reliance on numerical analysis and specific model parameters limits generality. Overall, it is a valuable addition to the literature on open quantum systems and non-Hermitian state control.
